tagline: Providing members with quality goods and services at the lowest possible prices
hero_kpi_rationale: Membership fees are at the core of Costco's business model, with 10% growth and fee increases.
company_description: Costco Wholesale Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, operates membership warehouses in the United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Japan, the United Kingdom, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Iceland, New Zealand, and Sweden. It offers merchandise, including sundries, dry groceries, candies, coolers, freezers, deli, liquor, and tobacco; non-food merchandise comprising appliances, small electronics, health and beauty aids, hardware, lawn and garden, sporting goods, tires, toys and seasonal, automotive, stamps, tickets, apparel, furniture, domestics, housewares, special order kiosks, and jewelry; and fresh food, such as meat, produce, service deli, and bakery products. The company also operates warehouse ancillary services, including gasoline, pharmacies, optical, food courts, hearing-aid centers, and tire installation centers. In addition, it operates e-commerce, business centers, travel, and other businesses. The company was formerly known as Costco Companies, Inc. and changed its name to Costco Wholesale Corporation in August 1999. Costco Wholesale Corporation was founded in 1976 and is based in Issaquah, Washington.

kpis.name: Comparable Sales Growth
kpis.explanation: Sales growth in warehouses open for more than one year
kpis.description: Measures sales growth in existing warehouses, reflecting member traffic and average basket size, excluding the impact of new store openings
kpis.signal: Indicator of organic business health excluding expansion

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue including merchandise, fuel, and services
kpis.description: Total revenue generated from merchandise sales (food and non-food), ancillary services (fuel, pharmacy, optical), and e-commerce, net of Executive member discounts
kpis.signal: Overall activity volume across all channels

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Gross margin as a percentage of net sales
kpis.description: Percentage margin after cost of goods sold, structurally low at Costco due to volume strategy, influenced by product mix and fuel proportion
kpis.signal: Core commercial profitability, reflecting pricing power

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Operating profit before taxes and financial expenses
kpis.description: Operating profit after deduction of all operating expenses (SG&A), including membership fees, reflecting the efficiency of the warehouse business model
kpis.signal: Overall operational profitability of the warehouse model

kpis.name: Membership Fee Revenue
kpis.explanation: Annual revenue generated from member fees
kpis.description: Fees paid by members (Business, Gold Star, Executive), a nearly pure-margin revenue stream that enables low prices on merchandise
kpis.signal: Highly predictable and profitable recurring revenue

kpis.name: Number of Warehouses
kpis.explanation: Total number of warehouses operated worldwide
kpis.description: Global network of operational warehouses (United States, Canada, Mexico, Asia, Europe), with a standardized format of approximately 147,000 square feet per site
kpis.signal: Physical network size and pace of geographic expansion

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Consolidated net profit after taxes (effective tax rate of 25.1%), distributed to shareholders and reinvested in growth, reflecting total economic performance

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total revenue of $275.235 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $2.77 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $2.183 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Proportion of net income distributed as dividends: 27.0% in the latest year.

kpis.name: E-commerce Sales Growth
kpis.description: Double-digit comparable growth in e-commerce sales, driven by operations in 8 countries (United States, Canada, Mexico, United Kingdom, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia)
kpis.signal: Strong digital momentum despite channel maturity

kpis.name: U.S. and Canada Revenue Concentration
kpis.explanation: Proportion of sales generated in the United States and Canada
kpis.description: 86% of sales and 84% of operating income come from North America, with California alone representing 26% of U.S. sales, creating concentration risk
kpis.signal: High geographic dependence, particularly on California

kpis.name: Net International Warehouse Openings
kpis.explanation: Net number of new warehouses outside the United States
kpis.description: 9 net international openings out of 24 total (Canada 2, Other 7), reflecting accelerated growth strategy in higher-potential, less competitive markets
kpis.signal: Acceleration of growth outside the home market

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares for the fiscal year. Used to assess the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Critical dependence on U.S. and Canadian operations
risks.summary: 86% of sales and 84% of operating income depend on the United States and Canada, with particular exposure to California (26% of U.S. sales), creating major vulnerability to local economic shocks.
risks.score_rationale: Ranked as the top risk factor with alarming language ('materially adversely affect'). Represents 86% of sales and 84% of operating income. California concentration (26% of U.S. sales) amplifies exposure. Any shock to these markets directly impacts consolidated results. Maximum structural industry risk. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Rising frequency and sophistication of cyberattacks and data breaches
risks.summary: Increasingly frequent and sophisticated cyberattacks threaten the security of sensitive data from millions of members, with risks of regulatory penalties, financial losses, and irreversible loss of trust.
risks.score_rationale: Highly alarming language regarding growing attack sophistication (ransomware, phishing). Explicit mention of existential consequences: loss of member trust, massive regulatory penalties, high remediation costs. Detailed section with attack vectors. Explicit upward trend. Cybersecurity is critical. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Failures in critical IT systems
risks.summary: Any major failure or delay in IT modernization projects could paralyze daily operations, degrade competitiveness, and compromise the reliability of financial reporting.
risks.score_rationale: IT systems described as vital for transactions, inventory, and decision-making. Mention of ongoing large-scale investments increasing exposure to project failures. Severe operational consequences but less existential than cyber risk. Firm language ('could materially adversely affect'). Technology is central but not maximal. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Non-compliance with strict and divergent data privacy regulations
risks.summary: Growing exposure to strict and divergent data protection regulations (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA) creates major legal, financial, and reputational risks in case of non-compliance or data breaches.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit citation of multiple regulations (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, PCI DSS) with potentially high penalties. Processing of sensitive data (health, payment) is core to the business model. Complexity increased by international expansion and remote work. High regulatory risk but not maximal as partially controllable. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Growing obstacles to warehouse network expansion
risks.summary: Geographic expansion is threatened by restrictive local regulations, community opposition to large-format stores, and intense competition for prime locations, potentially slowing growth.
risks.score_rationale: Strategic risk related to future growth: local regulations, community opposition, competition for premium sites, rising site costs. Concerned language but no immediate urgency. Impact on long-term growth. Significant industrial risk but not maximal. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Erosion of trust in the Kirkland Signature brand
risks.summary: Any perceived or actual failure in the quality, availability, or value perception of Kirkland Signature products could erode member loyalty and significantly reduce margins.
risks.score_rationale: Kirkland Signature represents a growing share of sales and margins (strategic private label). Clear statement that loss of acceptability would significantly impact revenue and profitability. Reputation is critical for member loyalty. Moderate language but strategic stakes. High reputational risk but not maximal. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Vulnerability to third-party payment systems and rising fees
risks.summary: Critical dependence on third-party payment providers exposes the company to fee increases, service interruptions, and costly PCI DSS compliance requirements, impacting margins and liquidity.
risks.score_rationale: Dependence on third-party providers for card payments (vital). Mention of potential fee increases, service outages, and complex PCI DSS compliance. Direct financial impact but manageable. Moderate capital risk, less central than major operational risks. (default score, to be refined)
